ticket.title: Add a standalone-build gate: every member must build with no harness path patches, from published crates only
ticket.description: Raised by the owner as a standing concern: 'individual tool use vs suite interoperability - both are important'. The layer gate protects interoperability (it forbids hidden coupling). NOTHING currently protects individual tool use, and the suite has already drifted: gaugeblock-workspace and gaugeblock-security are consumed by six member repositories and neither is published, so those members only build because the harness [patch.crates-io] table maps them to local paths. A checkout of sawhorse on its own cannot build. Measured 2026-11-06 against the crates.io API: of 51 package names, 5 are unpublished.\n\nShape: 'outfeed gate --standalone' (or miter) that, per member repository, resolves dependencies with the patch table disabled and fails when any dependency cannot be satisfied from the registry. It would have caught this drift the day the first unpublished dependency was introduced, and it is the guard that makes Law 2 (each repository compiles and is useful on its own) enforceable instead of aspirational. Cheapest implementation may be a cargo metadata pass with --offline and a temporary .cargo/config.toml that omits [patch.crates-io].
